slide_drafts.action_title: AI agents are becoming autonomous economic actors, but rigorous research on their real-stakes behavior is impossible through traditional institutions.
key_points: - AI agent market: $7.8B (2025) → $52.6B (2030), 46% CAGR (MarketsandMarkets)
- Agentic commerce projected at $300-500B in U.S. retail by 2030 (Bain)
- University IRBs lack expertise for AI economic experiments; real-asset studies blocked
- Corporate AI governance focused on liability avoidance, not exploratory research
- Zero published research on AI-to-AI autonomous economic transactions with real stakes
slide_drafts.speaker_notes: Good morning, Isozu-san. Thank you for making time to discuss something that I believe is critically important to SGE's mission. We are witnessing a historic inflection point. The AI agents market is projected to grow from roughly eight billion dollars today to over fifty billion by 2030—a forty-six percent compound annual growth rate. Bain estimates that by 2030, autonomous AI agents could influence up to five hundred billion dollars in U.S. retail transactions alone. These agents are no longer just analyzing data; they are making economic decisions. Yet here is the paradox: we have almost no rigorous empirical research on how these agents actually behave when real assets are at stake. Why? Because traditional institutions cannot run these experiments. University ethics boards lack the frameworks to approve real-money AI experiments—their guidelines were built for human subjects. And major tech companies like Google and OpenAI are constrained by accounting compliance and liability concerns that make such exploratory research impossible. This creates a dangerous blind spot just as AI agents become economic actors. Let me explain why this matters.

slide_drafts.action_title: Without this empirical data, policymakers and educators will design future AI institutions completely blind—a first-mover opportunity is slipping away.
key_points: - All 50 U.S. states introduced AI legislation in 2025; none informed by empirical agent behavior data
- Reinforcement-learning agents autonomously form cartels without communication (Wharton, NBER)
- 2010 Flash Crash: $1 trillion evaporated in 15 minutes from algorithmic cascade
- Future AI crises will unfold in minutes, not days—IMF, Bank of England warnings
- SGE's education infrastructure will teach a generation about economic systems we don't yet understand
slide_drafts.speaker_notes: Without empirical data on AI agent behavior, we are building the future blind. Consider this: in 2025 alone, all fifty U.S. states introduced AI-related legislation. But none of these policies are informed by actual empirical research on how AI agents behave in economic contexts. The risks are not theoretical. A recent NBER study from Wharton demonstrated that reinforcement-learning trading agents can autonomously develop cartel-like collusive behavior—without any communication or explicit programming. They simply learn that coordinated manipulation is profitable. We have seen what algorithmic cascades can do. In 2010, the Flash Crash wiped out one trillion dollars in market value in fifteen minutes. Regulators now warn that AI-driven crises will unfold even faster—in minutes or hours, not days. And here is where this connects to SGE's mission: you are building education infrastructure that will shape how the next generation understands economic systems. But we are teaching theories about economies that may no longer exist by the time students graduate. The window for first-mover research advantage is narrowing rapidly. On the next slide, I want to show you what we could build together.

todos.item: Find a specific 2024-2025 example of an AI agent causing unintended negative economic consequences outside of controlled research settings.

slide_drafts.action_title: Imagine a controlled research sandbox where AI agents trade real assets, forming emergent norms and institutions—generating data that shapes education and policy for decades.
key_points: - Research questions: How do AI agents form trust? Resolve disputes? Self-regulate markets?
- Emergent institution design: observe norm formation in controlled, real-stakes environment
- Cartel detection: identify collusion patterns before they appear in real markets
- Direct feed into SGE curriculum: teach students with data from actual AI economic behavior
- Long-term asset: research publications, policy white papers, educational case studies
slide_drafts.speaker_notes: Now imagine this: a controlled research environment where AI agents trade real assets—not simulated money, but actual value—and we can observe what emerges. This sandbox would answer questions that no institution in the world can currently address. How do AI agents form trust when there are no reputations to check? How do they resolve disputes when there is no court system? Do they spontaneously create institutions, or do they spiral into chaos? This research would be a goldmine for understanding emergent institution design. We could detect cartel formation patterns before they appear in real financial markets. We could study how norms develop—or fail to develop—in AI-mediated economies. And here is the direct connection to SGE: this data would feed directly into education. Imagine teaching economics students not from textbooks written about twentieth-century markets, but from real observations of twenty-first-century AI economic behavior. This is not just a research project. It is a long-term intellectual asset—publications, policy papers, educational case studies—that could position Sony and SGE as the definitive voice on AI economic behavior for decades. Let me show you exactly what we are proposing.

slide_drafts.action_title: The AI Agent Economy Competition is a blockchain-based research platform with real-asset stakes, targeting September 2025.
key_points: - Private blockchain: tamper-proof, verifiable research record (not crypto speculation)
- Real assets at stake: 16M JPY prize pool drives authentic agent behavior
- 100+ participating teams of AI agents competing in controlled economic scenarios
- Three-layer architecture: L0 (execution physics), L1 (institutions/norms), L2 (AI agents)
- September 2025 target: 8 months for collaborative design and infrastructure build
slide_drafts.speaker_notes: What we are proposing is the AI Agent Economy Competition—a blockchain-based research platform where AI agents compete in real economic scenarios with real assets at stake. Let me be clear about what 'blockchain' means here. This is not cryptocurrency speculation. The private blockchain serves as a tamper-proof, verifiable research record. Every transaction, every decision, every emergent behavior is permanently logged and auditable. This is the infrastructure of rigorous science, not financial engineering. The competition will feature over one hundred teams, each deploying AI agents that must navigate economic challenges. A sixteen-million-yen prize pool ensures authentic behavior—agents will be optimizing for real outcomes, not playing games. The architecture has three layers. Layer zero is the execution physics—the blockchain infrastructure itself. Layer one is where institutions and norms emerge. Layer two is where the AI agents operate. This separation lets us study each level independently while observing how they interact. We are targeting September 2025 for the first competition, giving us eight months for collaborative design. Now let me explain why this timing is uniquely favorable.

First movers in understanding AI economic behavior will shape the conversation for years to come. Eight months to September 2025 is actually ideal. Rushing would compromise the science. This timeline is both ambitious and achievable. But you may be wondering: why should you trust us to deliver? Let me share our track record.

slide_drafts.speaker_notes: I want to address the strategic fit question directly. This competition is designed to complement Soneium, not compete with it. Our private blockchain with custom tokens creates a controlled research environment. The tokens have no external trading value—they exist solely to create real stakes for AI agents within the experiment. If successful, we could explore integrating with Soneium's Layer 2, demonstrating blockchain utility for applications beyond cryptocurrency trading. This aligns perfectly with what Sota Watanabe has articulated as Soneium's vision: making blockchain infrastructure relevant for everyday life and enterprise use cases. For SGE specifically, the educational value is direct. The research outputs—studies on emergent AI norms, institution design principles, cartel formation patterns—become curriculum content. President Isozu has spoken about SGE's mission to create educational infrastructure that goes beyond traditional content. This is exactly that: original research that teaches students about the economic systems they will actually inhabit. And University of Tokyo students can participate directly—conducting research, publishing papers, building careers at the intersection of AI and economics. But I know safety concerns are paramount. Let me address those directly.

slide_drafts.action_title: Multiple validators, agent authentication, and pre-competition audits ensure this is a monitored research lab, not AI released into the wild.
key_points: - Multi-validator architecture: no single point of failure or manipulation
- Agent authentication: every agent verified, every transaction attributable
- Penalty systems: rule violations trigger automatic consequences within the experiment
- Pre-competition security audit: external review before any real assets deployed
- Private chain isolation: no connection to public networks or real financial markets
slide_drafts.speaker_notes: I want to be direct about safety because I know this is a priority for any Sony initiative. This is not AI released into the wild. This is a monitored research laboratory with multiple layers of control. First, the multi-validator architecture ensures no single entity—including us—can manipulate outcomes. Every rule change, every transaction validation requires consensus. Second, every AI agent is authenticated and every transaction is attributable. If an agent misbehaves, we know exactly which team is responsible and can trace every decision that led to the behavior. Third, the system includes built-in penalty mechanisms. Rule violations trigger automatic consequences within the experiment—this is how we study norm enforcement without external intervention. Before any real assets are deployed, we commit to a comprehensive pre-competition security audit by an external firm. And critically, this private blockchain is completely isolated. There is no connection to public networks, no interaction with real financial markets. What happens in the sandbox stays in the sandbox. This is research infrastructure designed with safety as a first principle. Now let me walk you through the implementation plan.
